requirements.text: The representative ESA (rear combination lamp with its LED modules, PCB, wiring and connector) shall fulfil the requirements of paragraph 6 of this Regulation (emissions and immunity in configurations other than REESS charging mode) for ESA type approval to be granted; paragraph 7 does not apply because the lamp is not used in REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid.
requirements.test_case: Review the test reports for radiated and conducted emission and immunity tests (paras 6.5, 6.6, 6.8, Annex 10) and confirm that all results meet paragraph 6.

requirements.text: Since the ESA is (part of) a light source, the ESA shall have the documentation specified in paragraph 3.2.10; without it, approval of the ESA under Regulation No. 10 shall not be granted.
requirements.test_case: Check that the approval file contains either an R37/R99/R128 approval number or a Technical Service non-interchangeability report for the LED light source.

requirements.text: In case of non-replaceable LED modules, a test report by a designated Technical Service shall be provided stating that the LED module/ESA is not mechanically interchangeable with any light source according to Regulation No. 37, No. 99 or No. 128.
requirements.test_case: Have the Technical Service inspect the LED module interface and compare it with the R37/R99/R128 light source caps, then issue the report.

requirements.text: In case of a replaceable LED light source approved under Regulation No. 128, the approval number granted to this light source under Regulation No. 128 shall be specified for the ESA.
requirements.test_case: Verify that the R128 approval number is quoted in the application and matches the marking on the light source.

requirements.text: An approval mark as described in paragraph 5.3 shall be affixed to every rear lamp (ESA) conforming to a type approved under UN R10.
requirements.test_case: Inspect production samples for the presence of the R10 approval mark.

requirements.text: The international approval mark shall be affixed in a conspicuous and easily accessible place on the ESA, as specified on the approval communication form.
requirements.test_case: Compare the mark location on the lamp with the location stated on the communication form.

requirements.text: The approval mark shall comprise a circle containing the letter "E", followed by the distinguishing number of the country granting the approval.
requirements.test_case: Visually inspect the mark for the circled "E" and the correct country number.

requirements.text: The approval mark shall comprise the number of this Regulation, followed by the letter "R", a dash and the approval number, placed to the right of the circle specified in paragraph 5.3.1.
requirements.test_case: Visually inspect the mark for "10R-" followed by the approval number to the right of the circle.

requirements.text: The R10 approval markings on the ESA (rear lamp) need not be visible when the ESA is installed in the vehicle.
requirements.test_case: Check on the drawing that the mark is on the lamp, accepting a location hidden when the lamp is installed.

requirements.text: The ESA (rear combination lamp with its LED modules, PCB and wiring) shall be designed, constructed and fitted so that the vehicle, in normal conditions of use, can comply with the requirements of UN R10.
requirements.test_case: Review the design and confirm that all applicable R10 ESA tests are passed.

requirements.text: The ESA shall be tested for radiated emissions, conducted emissions, immunity to radiated disturbances and immunity to conducted disturbances.
requirements.test_case: Check that the test plan and reports cover the radiated and conducted emission and immunity tests.

requirements.text: When measured by the method of Annex 7, the ESA broadband radiated emission limits shall be: 62 to 52 dBµV/m in the 30 to 75 MHz band, decreasing logarithmically with frequency above 30 MHz; 52 to 63 dBµV/m in the 75 to 400 MHz band, increasing logarithmically with frequency above 75 MHz; and constant at 63 dBµV/m in the 400 to 1,000 MHz band (Appendix 6).
requirements.test_case: Perform the Annex 7 (CISPR 25 ALSE) broadband measurement from 30 to 75 MHz and compare with the limit line.

requirements.text: On the ESA representative of its type, the measured broadband emission values, expressed in dBµV/m, shall be below the type approval limits.
requirements.test_case: Confirm that all measured broadband emission levels lie below the limit line across 30 to 1,000 MHz.

requirements.text: In case the ESA includes an electronic oscillator above 9 kHz, the ESA narrowband radiated emission limits measured by the method of Annex 8 shall be: 52 to 42 dBµV/m in the 30 to 75 MHz band, decreasing logarithmically with frequency above 30 MHz; 42 to 53 dBµV/m in the 75 to 400 MHz band, increasing logarithmically with frequency above 75 MHz; and constant at 53 dBµV/m in the 400 to 1,000 MHz band (Appendix 7).
requirements.test_case: Perform the Annex 8 narrowband measurement (average detector) from 30 to 75 MHz and compare with the limit line.

requirements.text: On the ESA representative of its type, the measured narrowband emission value, expressed in dBµV/m, shall be below the type approval limits.
requirements.test_case: Confirm that all measured narrowband levels lie below the limit line across 30 to 1,000 MHz.

requirements.text: Where the ESA does not include an electronic oscillator with an operating frequency greater than 9 kHz (e.g. passive resistor/linear LED drive), the ESA shall be deemed to comply with paragraph 6.6.2 and Annex 8 (narrowband emission).
requirements.test_case: Review the circuit schematic and component list to confirm that no oscillator or switching above 9 kHz is present.

requirements.text: The transient conducted emission of the ESA on 12/24 V supply lines, tested according to ISO 7637-2 as described in Annex 10, shall not exceed the maximum allowed pulse amplitudes of Table 1.
requirements.test_case: Measure the ISO 7637-2 transient emissions on the supply lines at switch-off/switching per Annex 10.

requirements.text: For a 12 V system ESA, the transient conducted emission pulse amplitude shall not exceed +75 V (positive) and -100 V (negative).
requirements.test_case: Measure the ISO 7637-2 positive pulse amplitude on the 12 V supply line.

requirements.text: For a 24 V system ESA, the transient conducted emission pulse amplitude shall not exceed +150 V (positive) and -450 V (negative).
requirements.test_case: Measure the ISO 7637-2 positive pulse amplitude on the 24 V supply line.

requirements.text: An ESA that is not switched, contains no switches or does not include an inductive load need not be tested for transient conducted emission and shall be deemed to comply with paragraph 6.7.
requirements.test_case: Review the schematic for switches, switching elements and inductive loads to justify the exemption.

requirements.text: The immunity of the ESA to electromagnetic radiation shall be tested by method(s) chosen from Annex 9, at the test severity of Table 2a in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 6,000 MHz band and at the minimum test level of Table 2b over the whole 20 to 6,000 MHz band.
requirements.test_case: Perform the Annex 9 radiated immunity test(s) at the Table 2a/2b levels while monitoring the lamp functions.

requirements.text: If tested by the stripline method, the ESA shall withstand 60 V/m in the 20 to 400 MHz range for over 90 per cent of the band.
requirements.test_case: Perform the stripline test at 60 V/m from 20 to 400 MHz and monitor the lamp functions.

requirements.text: If tested by the TEM cell method, the ESA shall withstand 75 V/m in the 20 to 200 MHz range for over 90 per cent of the band.
requirements.test_case: Perform the TEM cell test at 75 V/m from 20 to 200 MHz and monitor the lamp functions.

requirements.text: If tested by bulk current injection (BCI), the ESA shall withstand 60 mA in the 20 to 400 MHz range for over 90 per cent of the band.
requirements.test_case: Perform the BCI test at 60 mA from 20 to 400 MHz and monitor the lamp functions.

requirements.text: If tested in an ALSE, the ESA shall withstand 30 V/m from 80 to 2,000 MHz and 10 V/m from 2,000 to 6,000 MHz, for over 90 per cent of the band.
requirements.test_case: Perform the ALSE test at 30 V/m (80–2,000 MHz) and 10 V/m (2–6 GHz) and monitor the lamp functions.

requirements.text: If tested in a reverberation chamber, the ESA shall withstand 21 V/m from LUF to 2,000 MHz and 7 V/m from 2,000 to 6,000 MHz, for over 90 per cent of the band.
requirements.test_case: Perform the reverberation chamber test at 21 V/m and 7 V/m and monitor the lamp functions.

requirements.text: If tested by the stripline method, the minimum test level over the whole 20 to 400 MHz range shall be 50 V/m.
requirements.test_case: Verify from the test log that no frequency was tested below 50 V/m.

requirements.text: If tested by the TEM cell method, the minimum test level over the whole 20 to 200 MHz range shall be 62.5 V/m.
requirements.test_case: Verify from the test log that no frequency was tested below 62.5 V/m.

requirements.text: If tested by BCI, the minimum test level over the whole 20 to 400 MHz range shall be 50 mA.
requirements.test_case: Verify from the test log that no frequency was tested below 50 mA.

requirements.text: If tested in an ALSE, the minimum test level over the whole band shall be 25 V/m from 80 to 2,000 MHz and 8 V/m from 2,000 to 6,000 MHz.
requirements.test_case: Verify from the test log that the minimum levels of 25 V/m and 8 V/m were met.

requirements.text: If tested in a reverberation chamber, the minimum test level over the whole band shall be 18 V/m from LUF to 2,000 MHz and 6 V/m from 2,000 to 6,000 MHz.
requirements.test_case: Verify from the test log that the minimum levels of 18 V/m and 6 V/m were met.

requirements.text: During the radiated immunity tests of Annex 9 there shall be no degradation of performance of the immunity related functions (stop lamp and rear position lamp light output).
requirements.test_case: Monitor the stop and rear position lamp outputs (camera/photodetector) during exposure for any flicker, dimming or switch-off.

requirements.text: The immunity of the ESA to transients conducted along 12/24 V supply lines shall be tested according to ISO 16750-2 (starting profile) and ISO 7637-2 (pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a, 3b) as described in Annex 10, at the levels of Tables 3a and 3b. The results shall meet the ISO 16750-1 functional status classification for the starting profile and the ISO 7637-1 FPSC for the pulses.
requirements.test_case: Apply the starting profile and the ISO 7637-2 pulses to the supply lines and classify the lamp behaviour.

requirements.text: Where the ESA could be installed in vehicles with internal combustion engines started by a 12 V/24 V starter motor, the ESA shall withstand starting profile level II (12 V and 24 V) with 10 pulses. The functional status shall be class B for immunity related functions that must be operational during engine start, class C for other immunity related functions, and class D for functions not related to immunity related functions (e.g. reversing lamp).
requirements.test_case: Apply the ISO 16750-2 starting profile level II 10 times and assess the functional status of each lamp function.

requirements.text: For a 12 V system, the ESA shall withstand pulse 1 at -75 V for 500 pulses with FPSC III for both immunity related and non-immunity related functions.
requirements.test_case: Apply ISO 7637-2 pulse 1 at -75 V, 500 pulses, and verify FPSC III.

requirements.text: For a 24 V system, the ESA shall withstand pulse 1 at -450 V for 500 pulses with FPSC III for both immunity related and non-immunity related functions.
requirements.test_case: Apply ISO 7637-2 pulse 1 at -450 V, 500 pulses, and verify FPSC III.

requirements.text: For a 12 V system, the ESA shall withstand pulse 2a at +37 V for 500 pulses, with FPSC I for immunity related functions (stop/rear position lamp) and FPSC III for other functions.
requirements.test_case: Apply pulse 2a at +37 V, 500 pulses, and verify that the stop and position lamps are unaffected.

requirements.text: For a 24 V system, the ESA shall withstand pulse 2a at +37 V for 500 pulses, with FPSC I for immunity related functions and FPSC III for other functions.
requirements.test_case: Apply pulse 2a at +37 V, 500 pulses, and verify the FPSC per function.

requirements.text: For a 12 V system, the ESA shall withstand pulse 2b at +10 V for 10 pulses, with FPSC II for immunity related functions and FPSC III for other functions.
requirements.test_case: Apply pulse 2b at +10 V, 10 pulses, and verify the FPSC per function.

requirements.text: For a 24 V system, the ESA shall withstand pulse 2b at +20 V for 10 pulses, with FPSC II for immunity related functions and FPSC III for other functions.
requirements.test_case: Apply pulse 2b at +20 V, 10 pulses, and verify the FPSC per function.

requirements.text: For a 12 V system, the ESA shall withstand pulse 3a at -112 V for 1 h, with FPSC I for immunity related functions and FPSC III for other functions.
requirements.test_case: Apply pulse 3a at -112 V for 1 h and monitor the lamp outputs.

requirements.text: For a 24 V system, the ESA shall withstand pulse 3a at -150 V for 1 h, with FPSC I for immunity related functions and FPSC III for other functions.
requirements.test_case: Apply pulse 3a at -150 V for 1 h and monitor the lamp outputs.

requirements.text: For a 12 V system, the ESA shall withstand pulse 3b at +75 V for 1 h, with FPSC I for immunity related functions and FPSC III for other functions.
requirements.test_case: Apply pulse 3b at +75 V for 1 h and monitor the lamp outputs.

requirements.text: For a 24 V system, the ESA shall withstand pulse 3b at +150 V for 1 h, with FPSC I for immunity related functions and FPSC III for other functions.
requirements.test_case: Apply pulse 3b at +150 V for 1 h and monitor the lamp outputs.

requirements.text: ESAs approved under this Regulation shall be so manufactured as to conform to the type approved by meeting the requirements set forth in paragraph 6.
requirements.test_case: Take series samples of the rear lamp and repeat the paragraph 6 emission and immunity tests against the type-approval results.

requirements.text: For a production ESA taken from the series, the measured broadband electromagnetic emission levels shall not exceed the ESA broadband reference limits of paragraph 6.5.2.1 (62 to 52 dBµV/m in 30–75 MHz, 52 to 63 dBµV/m in 75–400 MHz, 63 dBµV/m in 400–1,000 MHz) by more than 4 dB (60 per cent).
requirements.test_case: Measure broadband radiated emission of a series lamp per Annex 7 and check that levels are at most 4 dB above the 6.5.2.1 limits.

requirements.text: For a production ESA taken from the series, the measured narrowband electromagnetic emission levels shall not exceed the ESA narrowband reference limits of paragraph 6.6.2.1 (52 to 42 dBµV/m in 30–75 MHz, 42 to 53 dBµV/m in 75–400 MHz, 53 dBµV/m in 400–1,000 MHz) by more than 4 dB (60 per cent).
requirements.test_case: Measure narrowband radiated emission of a series lamp per Annex 8 and check that levels are at most 4 dB above the 6.6.2.1 limits.

requirements.text: A production ESA taken from the series shall not exhibit any degradation relating to the direct control of the vehicle which could be observed by the driver or other road users (e.g. stop lamp or rear position lamp malfunction) when subjected to a field strength up to 80 per cent of the ESA immunity reference limits prescribed in paragraph 6.8.2.1.
requirements.test_case: Apply radiated immunity testing per Annex 9 at 80 % of the 6.8.2.1 levels to a series lamp and monitor the stop and rear position lamp outputs for any degradation.

requirements.text: A production component or STU taken from the series shall show no degradation of performance of immunity-related functions (stop lamp, rear position lamp) when subjected to conducted transient disturbances up to the levels given in paragraph 6.9.1.
requirements.test_case: Apply the Annex 10 conducted transient pulses at the 6.9.1 levels to a series lamp on its 12 V or 24 V supply and verify that the stop and rear position lamp functions are not degraded.

requirements.text: A production component or STU taken from the series shall not exceed the conducted transient emission levels given in paragraph 6.7.1.
requirements.test_case: Measure conducted transient emission of a series lamp on its supply lines per Annex 10 and compare the results with the 6.7.1 levels.

requirements.text: When measured by the method of Annex 7 with a 120 kHz bandwidth, the broadband electromagnetic radiation of the rear lamp ESA shall not exceed the ESA broadband reference limits E (dBµV/m) at frequency F (MHz): 30-75 MHz: E = 62 - 25.13 log (F/30); 75-400 MHz: E = 52 + 15.13 log (F/75); 400-1,000 MHz: E = 63. This applies unless the broadband exception of paragraph 6.10 covers the lamp's drive electronics (e.g. a passive resistor/linear LED drive).
requirements.test_case: Measure radiated broadband emission of the lamp per Annex 7 (ALSE, 30-1,000 MHz, 120 kHz bandwidth) and compare the peak values with the Appendix 6 limit line.

requirements.text: In case of an active electronic LED driver (oscillator, switch-mode or PWM, microcontroller or data bus), the narrowband electromagnetic radiation of the rear lamp ESA, when measured by the method of Annex 8 with a 120 kHz bandwidth, shall not exceed the ESA narrowband reference limits E (dBµV/m) at frequency F (MHz): 30-75 MHz: E = 52 - 25.13 log (F/30); 75-400 MHz: E = 42 + 15.13 log (F/75); 400-1,000 MHz: E = 53.
requirements.test_case: Measure radiated narrowband emission of the lamp per Annex 8 (ALSE, 30-1,000 MHz, 120 kHz bandwidth, average detector) and compare the values with the Appendix 7 limit line.

requirements.text: The ESA broadband emission limits (paragraph 6.5.2.1: 62 to 52 dBµV/m over 30–75 MHz decreasing logarithmically, 52 to 63 dBµV/m over 75–400 MHz increasing logarithmically, 63 dBµV/m constant over 400–1,000 MHz) apply throughout the frequency range 30 to 1,000 MHz for measurements in an ALSE or OATS.
requirements.test_case: Scan 30–1,000 MHz in both polarisations and check that all quasi-peak readings stay below the limit curve.

requirements.text: The narrowband emission limits for the rear lamp ESA apply throughout the frequency range 30 to 1,000 MHz for measurements in an absorber lined shielded enclosure (ALSE) or an open area test site (OATS).
requirements.test_case: Scan radiated emissions from 30 to 1,000 MHz in an ALSE or OATS and confirm that no narrowband emission exceeds the limit.

requirements.text: The rear lamp ESA shall be exposed to the radiated immunity disturbance over the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency range, with frequency steps and dwell times according to ISO 11452-1.
requirements.test_case: Perform the immunity test across 20 to 6,000 MHz with ISO 11452-1 step sizes and dwell times while monitoring the lamp functions.

requirements.text: In the 20 to 400 MHz frequency range, the immunity test signal applied to the rear lamp ESA shall be amplitude modulated (AM) with 1 kHz modulation and 80 per cent modulation depth.
requirements.test_case: Verify the signal generator settings (AM, 1 kHz, 80 %) for 20 to 400 MHz and monitor the lamp for malfunction.

requirements.text: In the 2,700 to 3,100 MHz frequency range, the immunity test signal applied to the rear lamp ESA shall be pulse modulated type PM2, with Ton 3 µs and period 3,333 µs.
requirements.test_case: Verify the PM2 settings (Ton 3 µs, period 3,333 µs) for 2,700 to 3,100 MHz and monitor the lamp for malfunction.

requirements.text: In the 380 to 2,700 MHz and 3,100 to 6,000 MHz frequency ranges, the immunity test signal applied to the rear lamp ESA shall be pulse modulated type PM3, with Ton 500 µs and period 1,000 µs.
requirements.test_case: Verify the PM3 settings (Ton 500 µs, period 1,000 µs) for 380 to 2,700 MHz and 3,100 to 6,000 MHz and monitor the lamp for malfunction.

requirements.text: The ESA (rear lamp LED modules and drive circuitry) shall be immune to transient disturbances conducted along the 12/24 V supply lines when test pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a and 3b according to ISO 7637-2 are applied to the supply lines and to the other connections of the ESA which may be operationally connected to supply lines (applies to the 12 V or 24 V version, whichever is supplied).
requirements.test_case: Apply ISO 7637-2 pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a and 3b to the supply and supply-connected lines of the lamp and check the lamp functions against the required functional status.

requirements.text: The ESA shall be immune to the starting profile according to ISO 16750-2 applied to the supply lines and to the other connections of the ESA which may be operationally connected to supply lines.
requirements.test_case: Apply the ISO 16750-2 starting profile to the lamp supply lines and verify the stop, rear position and reversing functions behave as required.

requirements.text: In case the ESA is exclusively reserved for mounting on electric vehicles (vehicles without 12 V/24 V starter motor), the ESA is not subject to the starting profile test according to ISO 16750-2.
requirements.test_case: Check the approval documentation for a restriction of use to electric vehicles before omitting the starting profile test.

requirements.text: The emission of transient conducted disturbances generated by the ESA on the 12/24 V supply lines and on other connections of the ESA which may be operationally connected to supply lines shall be limited, as measured according to ISO 7637-2.
requirements.test_case: Measure the conducted transient emissions on the lamp supply lines per ISO 7637-2 while switching the lamp functions and compare against the applicable limits.

requirements.text: The lamp shall have a space of sufficient size for the approval marking and the other markings defined in paragraphs 3.3.3.2. to 3.3.3.6.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the lamp drawing and sample to confirm there is a dedicated marking area large enough for all required markings.

requirements.text: All markings on the lamp shall be clearly legible and indelible.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the markings visually and perform a rub/durability check to confirm legibility and permanence.

requirements.text: The dimension "a" of the approval marking shall be at least 5 mm.
requirements.test_case: Measure the dimension "a" of the moulded or printed approval mark on the lamp.

requirements.text: The approval marking shall include the approval mark: a circle surrounding the letter "E" followed by the distinguishing number of the country that granted approval.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the marking for the circled E and the country number.

requirements.text: The approval marking shall include the four- to six-digit sequential number that forms part of the approval number.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the marking for the 4-6 digit sequential number and check it against the approval documentation.

requirements.text: The sequential number shall be placed close to the approval mark.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the marking layout to confirm the sequential number sits adjacent to the circled E.

requirements.text: The approval marking shall include the symbols identifying the approved lamp functions per paragraph 3.2.4: R1 (in case of steady rear position lamp) or R2 (in case of variable intensity rear position lamp); S1 (in case of steady stop lamp) or S2 (in case of variable intensity stop lamp); and AR for the reversing lamp.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the marking for the function symbols and compare them with the approved functions and classes.

requirements.text: The approval marking shall include the number of the Regulation followed by the letter "R" and the two digits of the series of amendments in force at the time of approval (e.g. 148R01).
requirements.test_case: Inspect the marking for "148R" followed by the correct series-of-amendments digits.

requirements.text: In case the lamp cannot be mounted on either side of the vehicle indiscriminately, it shall bear a horizontal arrow showing in which position the lamp is to be mounted.
requirements.test_case: Check the design for side dependency and, if side-specific, inspect the marking for the horizontal arrow.

requirements.text: For the rear position lamp (and rear end-outline marker lamp) function, the horizontal mounting arrow shall be directed outwards from the vehicle.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the arrow orientation relative to the intended mounting side.

requirements.text: In case the reversing lamp has a reduced light distribution for fitment of two reversing lamps, the horizontal mounting arrow shall be directed outwards from the vehicle.
requirements.test_case: For the reduced-distribution variant, inspect that the arrow points outboard.

requirements.text: In case the lamp may be used as part of an assembly of two independent lamps, the additional letter "D" shall be placed to the right side of the function symbol.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the marking for "D" to the right of the relevant function symbol.

requirements.text: In case the lamp is used as part of an interdependent lamp system, the additional letter "Y" shall be placed to the right side of the function symbol.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the marking for "Y" to the right of the relevant function symbol.

requirements.text: In case the lamp (e.g. the reversing lamp) has a reduced light distribution per paragraph 1.1. of Annex 3, it shall bear a vertical arrow starting from a horizontal segment and directed downwards.
requirements.test_case: For the reduced-distribution variant, inspect the marking for the downward vertical arrow on a horizontal segment.

requirements.text: The lamp shall bear the approval marking.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the production sample for the presence of the complete approval marking.

requirements.text: The lamp shall bear the trade name or mark of the applicant.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the lamp for the applicant's trade name or mark.

requirements.text: In case of non-replaceable LED light sources, the lamp is exempted from the marking of the light source category or categories.
requirements.test_case: Confirm the light sources are non-replaceable and that no category marking is needed.

requirements.text: The lamp shall bear a marking of its rated voltage(s) (e.g. 12V) or voltage range, because it has non-replaceable light sources (and, where applicable, an electronic light source control gear, a variable luminous intensity control or a secondary operating mode).
requirements.test_case: Inspect the lamp for the rated voltage or voltage range marking and compare it with the specification.

requirements.text: In case replaceable light source module(s) are used, each module shall bear the trade name or mark of the applicant.
requirements.test_case: Inspect each module for the applicant's trade name or mark.

requirements.text: In case replaceable light source module(s) are used, each module shall bear its specific identification code: the letters "MD" followed by the approval mark without the circle, plus additional symbols or characters where several non-identical modules are used. The module and lamp approval marks shall be from the same applicant.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the module for the MD code format and check the applicant against the lamp approval.

requirements.text: In case replaceable light source module(s) are used, each module shall bear its rated voltage(s) or voltage range.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the module for the rated voltage marking.

requirements.text: In case replaceable light source module(s) are used, the lamp shall bear the specific identification code of the module.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the lamp for the MD identification code matching the module.

requirements.text: In case replaceable light source module(s) are used, the lamp shall bear the rated voltage(s) or voltage range.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the lamp for the rated voltage marking.

requirements.text: In case an electronic light source control gear or variable luminous intensity control is part of the lamp but not included in the lamp body, it shall be marked with its identification number and the name of the manufacturer.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the external control unit for its identification number and manufacturer name.

requirements.text: The approval marking shall be placed on an inner or outer part (transparent or not) of the lamp that is not designed to be separated from the light-emitting transparent part of the lamp.
requirements.test_case: Review the assembly design to confirm the marked part cannot be separated from the outer lens.

requirements.text: The approval marking shall be visible when the lamp is fitted on the vehicle, or when a movable part such as the boot lid or a door is opened.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the lamp installed on the vehicle (with the boot lid open if needed) to confirm the approval marking is visible.

requirements.text: If the outer lens is designed to be separated from the main body, the approval marking shall be placed on both the detachable lens and the main body.
requirements.test_case: Check whether the lens is detachable and, if so, inspect both the lens and the housing for the approval marking.

requirements.text: In case the outer lens is used for several devices and bears different approval markings, the main body of each device shall bear only the approval marking of the function(s) of that device.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the main body marking to confirm it lists only its own functions.

requirements.text: The approval marking, the trade name or mark, the rated voltage marking, the module identification code and voltage (for lamps with replaceable modules) and, where applicable, the external control gear identification shall be affixed on the lamp.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the lamp assembly for the presence of all listed markings.

requirements.text: In case replaceable light source modules are used, the module markings (trade name, MD identification code, rated voltage) shall be affixed on the module itself.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the module component for its markings.

requirements.text: The trade name, light source category, rated voltage, light source module and control gear markings need not be visible when the lamp is fitted on the vehicle.
requirements.test_case: Confirm that only the approval marking is required to be visible when installed.

requirements.text: Where the grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps (R148 lamp functions and the R150 retro-reflector) comply with several UN Regulations, a single approval mark with the four- to six-digit sequential number may be affixed, located anywhere on the lamp assembly subject to paragraphs 3.3.5.1.1 and 3.3.5.1.2.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the single combined approval mark and its content against the approvals granted.

requirements.text: In case a single approval mark is used, it shall be visible after installation of the lamp.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the lamp installed on the vehicle for visibility of the single approval mark.

requirements.text: In case a single approval mark is used, no light-transmitting part of the grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps shall be removable without at the same time removing the approval mark.
requirements.test_case: Review the assembly design to confirm the lens and retro-reflector cannot be removed independently of the marked part.

requirements.text: The size of the components of a single approval mark shall not be less than the minimum size required for the smallest of the individual marks by the UN Regulations under which approval was granted (R148, R150).
requirements.test_case: Measure the mark component dimensions and compare them with the minimum sizes required by R148 and R150.

requirements.text: The requirements of sections 5 'General specifications' and 6 'Individual specifications' of UN R48 (series in force at application) that pertain to rear position, stop and reversing lamps for M1 vehicles shall be met where they can be verified at lamp type approval.
requirements.test_case: Check the lamp against the applicable R48 general and individual specifications, e.g. geometric visibility and colour, at component level.

requirements.text: The lamp shall be so designed and constructed that in normal conditions of use, and notwithstanding the vibrations to which it may be subjected, its satisfactory operation remains assured and it retains the characteristics prescribed by R148.
requirements.test_case: Perform a vibration/durability test, then re-verify photometry, colour and function.

requirements.text: In case the rear position lamp and/or stop lamp is approved as an assembly of two independent lamps marked 'D', this is permitted for these functions; the reversing lamp function cannot be approved as 'D'.
requirements.test_case: Check that a 'D' marking, if used, appears only on the rear position and/or stop lamp symbols.

requirements.text: In case the rear position lamp and/or stop lamp is part of an interdependent lamp system marked 'Y', this is permitted for these functions; the reversing lamp function cannot be approved as 'Y'.
requirements.test_case: Check that a 'Y' marking, if used, appears only on the rear position and/or stop lamp symbols.

requirements.text: A lamp approved as a rear position lamp is deemed to be also approved as a rear end-outline marker lamp.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the approval documentation for the rear position lamp approval.

requirements.text: A rear position lamp that is grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated with other functions may also be used as an end-outline marker lamp.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the lamp configuration and approval documentation.

requirements.text: In case the rear position lamp is reciprocally incorporated with the stop lamp using a common light source and is designed to operate permanently with an additional system regulating the intensity of the light emitted, this arrangement is permitted.
requirements.test_case: Review the circuit design and operating modes of the shared LEDs.

requirements.text: In case the rear position lamp is reciprocally incorporated with the stop lamp, these functions shall either (a) be provided by multiple light sources or (b) be intended for use on a vehicle equipped with a tell-tale indicating failure of the lamps.
requirements.test_case: Verify the LED circuit design for multiple independent light sources, or the declared tell-tale dependence in the communication document.

requirements.text: In case a manufacturer logo is incorporated in the rear position lamp, only one logo is permitted, built into the internal optical structure or outer lens texture within the apparent surface, and all requirements of the rear position lamp function shall still be fulfilled.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the logo design and re-verify the rear position lamp photometry and colour with the logo present.

requirements.text: In case a logo is incorporated in the rear position lamp, it shall be only the logo of the brand name of the vehicle manufacturer or body manufacturer.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the logo and the vehicle manufacturer statement.

requirements.text: In case a logo is incorporated in the rear position lamp, the enclosed light-emitting surface of the logo (transparent and non-transparent components), in the direction of the reference axis, shall not exceed 100 cm2.
requirements.test_case: Measure the projected enclosed area of the logo in the reference axis direction.

requirements.text: In case a logo is incorporated in the rear position lamp, the logo light-emitting surface need not be symmetrical by itself, notwithstanding paragraph 5.5.2 of UN R48.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the left and right lamp logo designs.

requirements.text: The stop lamp and reversing lamp functions shall not incorporate a logo.
requirements.test_case: Visually inspect the apparent surfaces of the stop and reversing lamps for any logo.

requirements.text: In a lamp function containing more than one light source, a group of LEDs wired so that the failure of any one of them causes all of them to stop emitting light shall be considered to be one light source.
requirements.test_case: Review the LED wiring schematic and identify the series strings treated as single light sources.

requirements.text: In case the lamp relies on internal failure provisions only, upon failure of any one light source in the rear position lamp or stop lamp, the light intensity shall still comply with the minimum intensities of the pertinent standard light distribution in Annex 3, and with all light sources illuminated the maximum intensities shall not be exceeded.
requirements.test_case: Disable each light source (LED string) in turn and measure photometry against the minimum values; measure maxima with all sources lit.

requirements.text: In case the lamp relies on a vehicle tell-tale, upon failure of any one light source in the rear position lamp or stop lamp, the lamp shall produce a signal for activation of a tell-tale indicating failure as per UN R48 (e.g. paragraphs 6.7.8 and 6.10.8), and the lamp is then only for use on vehicles fitted with such a tell-tale.
requirements.test_case: Simulate failure of each light source and verify that the failure signal output is generated.

requirements.text: In case of an R2 rear position lamp emitting more than the R1 maximum, upon failure of the variable intensity control the steady luminous intensity requirements of category R1 shall be fulfilled automatically.
requirements.test_case: Simulate failure of the variable intensity control and measure the intensities against the R1 limits.

requirements.text: In case of an S2 stop lamp emitting more than the S1 maximum, upon failure of the variable intensity control the steady luminous intensity requirements of category S1 shall be fulfilled automatically.
requirements.test_case: Simulate failure of the variable intensity control and measure the intensities against the S1 limits.

requirements.text: The lamp shall only be equipped with replaceable light sources approved under UN R37, R99 and/or R128 without use restriction, and/or light source modules, and/or non-replaceable light sources.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the light source design and documentation.

requirements.text: The lamp shall not generate radiated or power-line disturbances that cause a malfunction of other electric/electronic systems of the vehicle.
requirements.test_case: Perform radiated and conducted emission tests (e.g. per UN R10 ESA methods).

requirements.text: In case of replaceable light source modules, each module shall only be fittable in its designated and correct position.
requirements.test_case: Attempt to fit the module in incorrect positions and orientations.

requirements.text: In case of replaceable light source modules, each module shall only be removable with the use of tool(s).
requirements.test_case: Attempt to remove the module by hand without tools.

requirements.text: In case of replaceable light source modules, each module shall be tamperproof.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the module design for tamper resistance.

requirements.text: In case of replaceable light source modules, each module shall, regardless of the use of tools, not be interchangeable with any replaceable UN-approved light source or with any other module of different characteristics in the same lamp housing.
requirements.test_case: Attempt to interchange the modules of the R, S and AR functions and to fit standard light sources.

requirements.text: In case of replaceable light source modules, when a module is replaced by another module from the applicant bearing the same identification code, the photometric requirements of the lamp shall be met.
requirements.test_case: Swap in a second module with the same MD code and repeat the photometric measurements.

requirements.text: In case the lamp may be installed in more than one position or in a field of positions, the photometric requirements shall be met for each position or for the extreme positions of the reference axis field specified by the manufacturer.
requirements.test_case: Repeat the photometric measurements at each declared mounting position or extreme reference axis position.

requirements.text: Unless otherwise specified, the luminous intensities of the lamp functions shall be met with the light sources continuously lit.
requirements.test_case: Measure intensities with the functions continuously energised.

requirements.text: An intensity requirement for a particular direction of observation is deemed satisfied if it is met in a direction deviating by not more than 0.25° from that direction.
requirements.test_case: In case of a marginal result, evaluate intensities within ±0.25° of the test point.

requirements.text: Unless otherwise specified, the lamp shall meet the photometric and colorimetric requirements when supplied at 13.5 V (12 V system), or 28 V in case of a 24 V system rating.
requirements.test_case: Supply the lamp at 13.5 V during the photometric and colour tests.

requirements.text: In case the lamp is controlled by an electronic light source control gear or variable intensity control, the lamp shall meet the requirements when operated as specified by the applicant.
requirements.test_case: Operate the lamp with the declared control gear and settings during the tests.

requirements.text: In case the lamp is not controlled by an electronic light source control gear or variable intensity control and uses non-replaceable light sources or light source modules, the lamp shall meet the requirements when operated as specified by the applicant.
requirements.test_case: Operate the lamp at the declared supply conditions during the tests.

requirements.text: The luminous intensity of each of the two samples on the reference axis (HV) shall be not less than the minimum specified in the paragraph 5 table for each function (rear position lamp, stop lamp, reversing lamp).
requirements.test_case: Measure the HV intensity of each function on two samples with a goniophotometer.

requirements.text: The luminous intensity of each function shall, in no direction where the lamp is visible, exceed the maximum specified in the paragraph 5 table for that function.
requirements.test_case: Scan the full visible field of each function and compare the peak intensity with the maximum.

requirements.text: Outside the reference axis, the luminous intensity of each function shall be not less than the minimum of the paragraph 5 table multiplied by the percentage given in the pertinent Annex 3 light distribution figure (Figure A3-I for R and S), or not less than the cd value given in the figure (Figure A3-V for AR), for each direction.
requirements.test_case: Measure all grid points of Figure A3-I or A3-V and compare with the computed minima.

requirements.text: Within the angles of geometric visibility defined in Annex 2, the luminous intensity of each function shall be not less than the geometric visibility minimum specified in the paragraph 5 table.
requirements.test_case: Measure intensity across the Annex 2 visibility field of each function.

requirements.text: The provisions of Annex 3 on local variations of intensity shall be observed for each function.
requirements.test_case: Check intensities between grid points against the Annex 3 uniformity criteria.

requirements.text: In case of an assembly of two independent lamps marked 'D' with the same function, the assembly shall comply with the maximum intensity requirement when all lamps are lit together.
requirements.test_case: Measure the maximum intensity with both lamps of the assembly lit.

requirements.text: In case of an assembly of two independent lamps marked 'D' with the same function, the assembly shall comply with the minimum intensity requirement when either lamp has failed.
requirements.test_case: Measure the minimum intensities with each lamp of the assembly switched off in turn.

requirements.text: In case of an interdependent lamp system ('Y'), the system shall meet the requirements when all its interdependent lamps are operated together.
requirements.test_case: Measure photometry with all interdependent lamps of the system operated together.

requirements.text: In case an interdependent system providing the rear position lamp is partly mounted on a movable component (e.g. tailgate), the interdependent lamp(s) specified by the applicant shall meet the outboard geometric visibility, colorimetric and photometric requirements at all fixed positions of the movable component.
requirements.test_case: Measure the specified lamp(s) at each fixed position of the movable component.

requirements.text: In case an interdependent system providing the rear position lamp is partly mounted on a movable component, the inboard geometric visibility requirement is deemed satisfied if the specified interdependent lamp(s) still conform to the photometric values in the field of light distribution at all fixed positions of the movable component.
requirements.test_case: Verify the light distribution grid values at all fixed positions of the movable component.

requirements.text: In case of an R2 rear position lamp or S2 stop lamp, the variable intensity control shall not generate signals causing luminous intensities outside the range specified in paragraph 5.
requirements.test_case: Drive the variable intensity control over its full range and measure the min/max intensities.

requirements.text: In case of an R2 or S2 lamp with a variable intensity control depending only on daytime and night-time conditions, the control shall not cause intensities exceeding the steady (R1/S1) maximum under night-time conditions.
requirements.test_case: Set the control to night-time mode and measure the maximum intensities.

requirements.text: In case of an R2 or S2 lamp with any other variable intensity control system, the control shall not cause intensities exceeding the steady (R1/S1) maximum under standard conditions (good visibility, MOR > 2,000 m, clean lens).
requirements.test_case: Set the control to the standard-conditions input and measure the maximum intensities.

requirements.text: The luminous intensities of each function shall comply when tested according to Annex 8.
requirements.test_case: Run the Annex 8 photometric test sequence on the samples.

requirements.text: The colour of the light emitted by each function, measured inside the field of its light distribution grid in Annex 3, shall meet the colour prescribed for that function (red for the rear position and stop lamps, white for the reversing lamp).
requirements.test_case: Measure chromaticity coordinates across each function's light distribution grid with a spectroradiometer.

requirements.text: Outside the field of the light distribution grid, no sharp variation of colour of the light emitted shall be observed.
requirements.test_case: Visually and colorimetrically inspect the colour outside the grid field for abrupt changes.

requirements.text: In case the rear position lamp is reciprocally incorporated with the stop lamp, a luminous intensity of up to 60 cd is permitted for the rear position lamp below a plane forming an angle of 5° with and downward from the horizontal plane.
requirements.test_case: Measure rear position lamp intensity below 5°D and check it does not exceed 60 cd.

requirements.text: For rear position lamps of category R1 or R2, the luminous intensity shall be at least 4 cd on the reference axis (HV), and outside the reference axis at least the product of 4 cd and the percentage of the standard light distribution of Figure A3-I for each direction.
requirements.test_case: Measure intensity at HV and at all Figure A3-I grid points and compare with the minimum values.

requirements.text: In case of a steady rear position lamp (R1) used as a single lamp, the luminous intensity shall not exceed 17 cd in any direction in which the lamp is visible.
requirements.test_case: Goniophotometric scan to find the maximum intensity and compare with 17 cd.

requirements.text: In case of a steady rear position lamp (R1) marked "D", the luminous intensity shall not exceed 8.5 cd in any direction in which the lamp is visible.
requirements.test_case: Goniophotometric scan to find the maximum intensity and compare with 8.5 cd.

requirements.text: In case of a variable intensity rear position lamp (R2) used as a single lamp, the luminous intensity shall not exceed 42 cd in any direction in which the lamp is visible.
requirements.test_case: Goniophotometric scan at the highest intensity setting and compare the maximum with 42 cd.

requirements.text: In case of a variable intensity rear position lamp (R2) marked "D", the luminous intensity shall not exceed 21 cd in any direction in which the lamp is visible.
requirements.test_case: Goniophotometric scan at the highest intensity setting and compare the maximum with 21 cd.

requirements.text: Within the angles of geometric visibility of Table A2-1 for rear position lamps (R1, R2), the luminous intensity shall be at least 0.05 cd. These angles are 45° inboard / 80° outboard horizontally (20°/80° below the H-plane for lamps mounted with the H-plane below 750 mm) and 15° above / 15° below vertically (15°/5° for mounting height below 750 mm).
requirements.test_case: Measure intensity over the full geometric visibility field and verify ≥0.05 cd everywhere.

requirements.text: The colour of the light emitted by the rear position lamp shall be red.
requirements.test_case: Colorimetric measurement of the emitted light and check against the red chromaticity limits.

requirements.text: For stop lamps of category S1 or S2, the luminous intensity shall be at least 60 cd on the reference axis (HV), and outside the reference axis at least the product of 60 cd and the percentage of the standard light distribution of Figure A3-I for each direction.
requirements.test_case: Measure intensity at HV and at all Figure A3-I grid points and compare with the minimum values.

requirements.text: In case of a steady stop lamp (S1) used as a single lamp, the luminous intensity shall not exceed 260 cd in any direction in which the lamp is visible.
requirements.test_case: Goniophotometric scan to find the maximum intensity and compare with 260 cd.

requirements.text: In case of a steady stop lamp (S1) marked "D", the luminous intensity shall not exceed 130 cd in any direction in which the lamp is visible.
requirements.test_case: Goniophotometric scan to find the maximum intensity and compare with 130 cd.

requirements.text: In case of a variable intensity stop lamp (S2) used as a single lamp, the luminous intensity shall not exceed 730 cd in any direction in which the lamp is visible.
requirements.test_case: Goniophotometric scan at the highest intensity setting and compare the maximum with 730 cd.

requirements.text: In case of a variable intensity stop lamp (S2) marked "D", the luminous intensity shall not exceed 365 cd in any direction in which the lamp is visible.
requirements.test_case: Goniophotometric scan at the highest intensity setting and compare the maximum with 365 cd.

requirements.text: In case of a steady stop lamp (S1), the luminous intensity shall be at least 0.3 cd within the angles of geometric visibility of Table A2-1. These angles are 45° inboard / 45° outboard horizontally (20°/45° below the H-plane for lamps mounted with the H-plane below 750 mm) and 15° above / 15° below vertically (15°/5° for mounting height below 750 mm).
requirements.test_case: Measure intensity over the full geometric visibility field and verify ≥0.3 cd everywhere.

requirements.text: In case of a variable intensity stop lamp (S2), the luminous intensity within the angles of geometric visibility of Table A2-1 shall be at least 0.3 cd under day conditions and at least 0.07 cd under night conditions. These angles are 45°/45° horizontally (20°/45° below the H-plane if mounted below 750 mm) and 15°/15° vertically (15°/5° if mounted below 750 mm).
requirements.test_case: Measure intensity over the geometric visibility field at the day and night intensity settings and compare with 0.3 cd and 0.07 cd.

requirements.text: The colour of the light emitted by the stop lamp shall be red.
requirements.test_case: Colorimetric measurement of the emitted light and check against the red chromaticity limits.

requirements.text: In case the reversing lamp is intended to be installed on a vehicle exclusively in a pair of devices (reduced light distribution), the photometric intensity may be verified only up to an angle of 30° inwards, where a luminous intensity of at least 25 cd shall be satisfied.
requirements.test_case: Measure the reversing lamp intensity at 30° inwards and verify ≥25 cd.

requirements.text: For the reversing lamp (AR), the luminous intensity shall be at least 80 cd on the reference axis (HV), and outside the reference axis at least the values derived from the standard light distribution of Figure A3-V.
requirements.test_case: Measure intensity at HV and at all Figure A3-V grid points and compare with the minimum values.

requirements.text: For the reversing lamp (AR), the luminous intensity shall not exceed 300 cd in directions in or above the H-plane, 600 cd in directions below the H-plane down to 5°D, and 8,000 cd in directions below 5°D.
requirements.test_case: Goniophotometric scan in and above the H-plane and compare the maximum with 300 cd.

requirements.text: The colour of the light emitted by the reversing lamp shall be white.
requirements.test_case: Colorimetric measurement of the reversing lamp light and check against the white chromaticity limits.

requirements.text: Production lamps (rear position, stop and reversing lamp functions) shall be manufactured so as to conform to the type approved under UN R148, including the specific technical requirements of paragraph 5.
requirements.test_case: Compare randomly selected production lamps with the approved type documentation and re-test them to paragraph 5 requirements.

requirements.text: For production lamps, no measured photometric value of the rear position, stop or reversing lamp function shall deviate unfavourably by more than 20 per cent from the values prescribed in UN R148.
requirements.test_case: Measure luminous intensities of randomly selected production lamps per paragraph 4.8 and check that each value is within 20 per cent of the prescribed limits.

requirements.text: For the minimum values required throughout the fields of Annexes 2 and 3, production lamps shall meet the equivalent values of Table 12. A required minimum of 7∙10^-1 cd corresponds to 5∙10^-1 cd (20 %) and 3∙10^-1 cd (30 %). 6∙10^-1 cd corresponds to 4∙10^-1 cd (20 %) and 2∙10^-1 cd (30 %). 3∙10^-1 cd corresponds to 2∙10^-1 cd (20 %) and 1∙10^-1 cd (30 %). 7∙10^-2 cd corresponds to 5∙10^-2 cd (20 %) and 3∙10^-2 cd (30 %). 5∙10^-2 cd corresponds to 3∙10^-2 cd (20 %) and 2∙10^-2 cd (30 %); this last row covers the minimum within the angles of geometric visibility for the R1/R2 and S1/S2 functions.
requirements.test_case: Measure the low-intensity points within the geometric visibility field of production samples and compare them with the Table 12 equivalent values.

requirements.text: Each lamp function (rear position lamp R1/R2 and stop lamp S1/S2) shall provide at least the minimum angles of geometric visibility, horizontal and vertical, given in Table A2-1 (Part A, Figures A2-I). The angles shown apply to a lamp mounted on the right side of the vehicle and are mirrored for a left-side lamp.
requirements.test_case: Goniometric check of the light-emitting surface visibility over the specified angular field for the right-hand and left-hand variants.

requirements.text: The rear position lamp (R1, R2) shall have minimum horizontal angles of geometric visibility of 45° inboard and 80° outboard. For lamps mounted with the H-plane below 750 mm, the inboard angle below the H-plane may be reduced to 20° (20°/80°).
requirements.test_case: Verify on a goniometer that the apparent surface remains visible from 45° inboard to 80° outboard (20° inboard below H-plane if the mounting height is below 750 mm).

requirements.text: The rear position lamp (R1, R2) shall have minimum vertical angles of geometric visibility of 15° above and 15° below the H-plane. For lamps to be installed with the H-plane at a mounting height of less than 750 mm, the angle below may be reduced to 5° (15°/5°).
requirements.test_case: Verify on a goniometer that the apparent surface remains visible from 15° up to 15° down (5° down if the mounting height is below 750 mm).

requirements.text: The stop lamp (S1, S2) shall have minimum horizontal angles of geometric visibility of 45° inboard and 45° outboard. For lamps mounted with the H-plane below 750 mm, the inboard angle below the H-plane may be reduced to 20° (20°/45°).
requirements.test_case: Verify on a goniometer that the stop lamp apparent surface remains visible from 45° inboard to 45° outboard (20° inboard below H-plane if the mounting height is below 750 mm).

requirements.text: The stop lamp (S1, S2) shall have minimum vertical angles of geometric visibility of 15° above and 15° below the H-plane. For lamps to be installed with the H-plane at a mounting height of less than 750 mm, the angle below may be reduced to 5° (15°/5°).
requirements.test_case: Verify on a goniometer that the stop lamp apparent surface remains visible from 15° up to 15° down (5° down if the mounting height is below 750 mm).

requirements.text: Where the rear position lamp is also used as a rear end-outline marker lamp (RM1, RM2), it shall have minimum horizontal angles of geometric visibility of 0° inboard and 80° outboard.
requirements.test_case: Goniometric check of apparent surface visibility from 0° to 80° outboard.

requirements.text: Where the rear position lamp is also used as a rear end-outline marker lamp (RM1, RM2), it shall have minimum vertical angles of geometric visibility of 15° above and 15° below the H-plane. For lamps to be installed with the H-plane at a mounting height of less than 750 mm, the angle below may be reduced to 5° (15°/5°).
requirements.test_case: Goniometric check of apparent surface visibility from 15° up to 15° down (5° down if the mounting height is below 750 mm).

requirements.text: For the rear position lamp (R1/R2), the stop lamp (S1/S2) and the reversing lamp, the minimum luminous intensities required in the various directions of measurement shall be the percentages shown in the applicable standard light distribution figure, applied to the minimum intensity required for the function. Each resulting value shall be mathematically rounded down to three significant digits. Directions are referenced to H = 0°, V = 0°, which is the reference axis through the centre of reference.
requirements.test_case: Goniophotometer measurement at each grid point, compared with the figure percentage of the table minimum rounded down to three significant digits.

requirements.text: Where the rear position lamp (R1/R2) is intended to be installed at a mounting height of 750 mm or less above the ground (using the H plane specified by the manufacturer), its photometric intensity is verified only up to an angle of 5° downwards.
requirements.test_case: Check the declared mounting height; if it is 750 mm or less, limit the downward photometric verification to V = 5° down.

requirements.text: Where the stop lamp of category S1 or S2 is intended to be installed at a mounting height of 750 mm or less above the ground (using the H plane specified by the manufacturer), its photometric intensity is verified only up to an angle of 5° downwards.
requirements.test_case: Check the declared mounting height; if it is 750 mm or less, limit the downward photometric verification of the stop lamp to V = 5° down.

requirements.text: Within the field of light distribution shown as a grid, the luminous intensity of the rear position lamp and the stop lamp in each direction of a part of the field formed by the grid lines shall be at least the lowest minimum value (as a percentage) shown on the grid lines surrounding that direction.
requirements.test_case: Scan intermediate directions between the grid lines with a goniophotometer and confirm each value is at least the lowest surrounding grid minimum.

requirements.text: For the reversing lamp, if visual examination reveals substantial local variations of intensity, no intensity measured between two directions of measurement shall be below 50 per cent of the lower of the two minimum intensities prescribed for those directions.
requirements.test_case: Visually inspect the beam; if local variations are seen, measure between adjacent measuring points and confirm each value is at least 50% of the lower prescribed minimum.

requirements.text: In case of an R1 (steady) or an R2 (variable intensity) rear position lamp, the luminous intensity in each direction of measurement shall be at least the percentage given in Figure A3-I of the minimum luminous intensity required in Table 3.
requirements.test_case: Goniophotometric measurement at all Figure A3-I points, compared with the Figure A3-I percentages of the Table 3 minimum.

requirements.text: In case of an S1 (steady) or an S2 (variable intensity) stop lamp, the luminous intensity in each direction of measurement shall be at least the percentage given in Figure A3-I of the minimum luminous intensity required in Table 7, i.e. 60 cd.
requirements.test_case: Goniophotometric measurement at all Figure A3-I points, compared with the Figure A3-I percentages of 60 cd.

requirements.text: In case of a reversing lamp with standard light distribution, the luminous intensity at each measuring point of Figure A3-V (in degrees from the reference axis) shall be at least the minimum intensity in cd shown in Figure A3-V.
requirements.test_case: Goniophotometric measurement at each Figure A3-V measuring point, compared with the cd minima of Figure A3-V.

requirements.text: From a mechanical and geometric standpoint, the differences of mass-produced rear combination lamps (rear position, stop and reversing lamp functions) from the approved type shall not exceed inevitable manufacturing deviations within the requirements of this Regulation.
requirements.test_case: Inspect and measure dimensions and geometry of randomly selected production lamps and compare them with the approved type drawings and tolerances.

requirements.text: The photometric performance of any mass-produced lamp chosen at random (rear position lamp, stop lamp and reversing lamp functions), tested according to paragraph 4.8 with the non-replaceable LED light sources or light source modules present in the lamp, shall meet the photometric requirements of this Regulation, so that the conformity of production is not contested.
requirements.test_case: Measure luminous intensities of a randomly selected production lamp per function at the Annex 3 grid points according to paragraph 4.8 and compare with the paragraph 5 values and the paragraph 6.1.3 deviation limits.

requirements.text: The chromaticity coordinates of the light emitted by mass-produced lamps (red for the rear position and stop lamp functions, white for the reversing lamp function) shall be complied with when tested under the conditions of paragraph 4.9.
requirements.test_case: Measure the chromaticity coordinates of each function of a randomly selected production lamp within the light distribution grid per paragraph 4.9 and check them against the colour limits.

requirements.text: For the reversing lamp (non-incandescent, LED light sources), the luminous intensities measured after 1 minute and after 10 minutes of operation shall comply with the minimum and maximum requirements.
requirements.test_case: Measure the reversing lamp light distribution goniophotometrically after 1 min and after 10 min of operation and compare it with the minimum and maximum limits.

requirements.text: For the rear position lamp and the stop lamp (non-incandescent, LED light sources), the luminous intensities measured after 1 min and either after 30 minutes of operation or after photometric stability has occurred shall comply with the minimum and maximum requirements.
requirements.test_case: Measure the rear position and stop lamp intensities after 1 min and after 30 min (or at photometric stability) and compare them with the minimum and maximum limits.

requirements.text: The rear position lamp shall comply with its luminous intensity requirements 4 seconds after switch ON (reference coordinate HV).
requirements.test_case: Record the HV intensity 4 s after switch-on and scale the distribution to check against the min/max limits.

requirements.text: The stop lamp shall comply with its luminous intensity requirements 0.2 seconds after switch ON (reference coordinate HV).
requirements.test_case: Record the HV intensity 0.2 s after switch-on with a fast photometer and check it against the min/max limits.

requirements.text: The reversing lamp shall comply with its luminous intensity requirements 0.2 seconds after switch ON (reference coordinate HV).
requirements.test_case: Record the HV intensity 0.2 s after switch-on with a fast photometer and check it against the min/max limits.

requirements.text: In case a lamp function uses LED technology only, the lamp function is deemed to comply with the corresponding intensity requirements at all points in time if the values measured according to paragraph 1.2 of Annex 8 are compliant.
requirements.test_case: Confirm by inspection that each function uses LEDs only and that the measurements under paragraph 1.2 pass.

requirements.text: In case of doubt (e.g. unexpected run-up behaviour), the minimum intensity requirements of each lamp function shall be met at all points in time, starting at the point in time listed in Table A8-1 (0.2 s for stop and reversing lamps, 4 s for the rear position lamp) and ending when photometric stability is reached.
requirements.test_case: Continuously record the HV intensity from the Table A8-1 time until photometric stability and verify that it never falls below the minimum.

requirements.text: The retro-reflector shall have a space large enough for either the Unique Identifier and the other markings defined in paragraph 3.3.4.2, or the approval marking and the other markings defined in paragraph 3.3.4.2.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the drawing and a sample to confirm there is a marking area large enough for the UI or the approval marking plus the other markings.

requirements.text: All markings on the retro-reflector shall be clearly legible and indelible.
requirements.test_case: Visually inspect the markings and rub them with water- and petrol-soaked cloths to check they stay legible.

requirements.text: The size of the approval marking shall be based on the value of 'a' defined in Table 1. For a retro-reflector for motor vehicles of Class IA (independent) or Class IB (combined with other signal lamps which are not watertight), the minimum 'a' is 5 mm.
requirements.test_case: Measure 'a' on the approval mark and check it is at least 5 mm.

requirements.text: The approval marking shall contain the approval mark: a circle surrounding the letter 'E', followed by the distinguishing number of the country that granted approval.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the marking for the circled 'E' and the country number.

requirements.text: The approval marking shall contain the four- to six-digit sequential number that forms part of the approval number.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the marking for the sequential number and check it against the approval communication.

requirements.text: The sequential number of the approval number shall be placed close to the approval mark.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the marking to confirm the sequential number sits next to the circled E.

requirements.text: In case the lamp containing the retro-reflector is watertight, the approval marking shall contain the class symbol 'IA' (retro-reflector for motor vehicles, independent).
requirements.test_case: Inspect the marking for the symbol 'IA'.

requirements.text: In case the lamp containing the retro-reflector is not watertight, the approval marking shall contain the class symbol 'IB' (retro-reflector for motor vehicles combined with other signal lamps which are not watertight).
requirements.test_case: Inspect the marking for the symbol 'IB'.

requirements.text: The approval marking shall contain the Regulation number '150', followed by the letter 'R' and the two digits of the series of amendments in force when the approval was issued (e.g. 150R01).
requirements.test_case: Inspect the marking for '150R' followed by the series digits.

requirements.text: The approval marking may be replaced by the Unique Identifier, if available; in that case the UI mark shall follow the format shown in Figure I.
requirements.test_case: If a UI is used, compare the marked UI with the Figure I format and check the database entry.

requirements.text: The retro-reflector shall bear the trade name or mark of the applicant.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the sample for the applicant's trade name or mark.

requirements.text: A Class IA or IB retro-reflector shall bear the word 'TOP' written horizontally on the highest part of the illuminating surface, if this is needed to determine without ambiguity the angle(s) of rotation prescribed by the manufacturer.
requirements.test_case: Check whether the photometry depends on rotation and, if so, inspect for 'TOP' on the uppermost part of the illuminating surface.

requirements.text: The approval marking or Unique Identifier, and the markings of paragraph 3.3.4, shall be clearly legible on the retro-reflective device.
requirements.test_case: Visually inspect the sample to confirm all markings are legible on the device.

requirements.text: Where the grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps (rear position, stop and reversing lamps with the retro-reflector) comply with several UN Regulations, a single approval mark with the four- to six-digit sequential number, or a single Unique Identifier, may be affixed anywhere on the lamp assembly, subject to the conditions of paragraphs 3.3.6.1.1 and 3.3.6.1.2.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the single mark on the assembly and check that it covers all applicable approvals.

requirements.text: If a single approval mark or UI is used on the grouped/combined/reciprocally incorporated lamps, it shall be visible after the lamp is installed on the vehicle.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the lamp installed on the vehicle, or a mock-up, to confirm the mark is visible.

requirements.text: If a single approval mark or UI is used, no light-transmitting part of the grouped/combined/reciprocally incorporated lamps (e.g. the outer lens or the retro-reflector) shall be removable without also removing the approval mark with its sequential number or the UI.
requirements.test_case: Review the design and do a disassembly check that the mark sits on a part that cannot be separated from the light-transmitting parts.

requirements.text: The components of a single approval mark shall be no smaller than the minimum size required for the smallest of the individual marks by the UN Regulations under which approval was granted (R150, R148).
requirements.test_case: Measure the mark components and compare them with the minimum sizes required by R150 and R148.

requirements.text: The retro-reflector shall be so constructed that it functions satisfactorily and continues to do so in normal use.
requirements.test_case: Verify retained photometric and colorimetric compliance after the prescribed resistance tests (heat, water, corrosion, fuel).

requirements.text: The retro-reflector must not have any defect in design or manufacture that is detrimental to its efficient operation or to its maintenance in good condition.
requirements.test_case: Visually inspect the samples and review the design for defects affecting operation or maintenance.

requirements.text: The components of the retro-reflector, or parts thereof, shall not be capable of being easily dismantled.
requirements.test_case: Attempt manual disassembly of the retro-reflector components without tools and confirm they cannot easily be separated.

requirements.text: The outer surface of the retro-reflector shall be easy to clean.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the outer surface and confirm it can be cleaned easily.

requirements.text: The outer surface of the retro-reflector shall not be rough, and any protuberances it may exhibit shall not prevent easy cleaning.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the outer surface visually and by touch for roughness and for protuberances that hinder cleaning.

requirements.text: There shall be no access to the inner surface of the retro-reflector when in normal use.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the mounted lamp assembly and confirm the inner (prism) surface cannot be reached in normal use.

requirements.text: In case the retro-reflector consists of a combined retro-reflecting optical unit and filter (e.g. a colourless optical unit behind the red outer lens acting as filter), the optical unit and filter must be so designed that they cannot be separated under normal conditions of use.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the assembly and attempt separation of the optical unit and filter under normal use conditions; confirm they cannot be separated.

requirements.text: The retro-reflecting optical unit and any filter shall not be coloured by means of paint or varnish.
requirements.test_case: Inspect and review the material specification to confirm the red colour is from the material (mass-tinted), not paint or varnish.

requirements.text: When the retro-reflector is illuminated by CIE Standard Illuminant A with an angle of divergence of 1/3° and an illumination angle β1 = β2 = 0°, the trichromatic coordinates of the reflected luminous intensity shall be within the UN R48 limits for red night-time retro-reflected light. If 0° produces a colourless surface reflection, the angle β1 = -5°, β2 = 0° of Annex 4 Part 1 paragraph 1.1 shall be used.
requirements.test_case: Measure the chromaticity of the retro-reflected light under Illuminant A at 1/3° divergence and 0°/0° (or -5°/0°) illumination, and compare with the R48 red limits.

requirements.text: The Class IA or IB retro-reflector, when tested according to paragraph 5.1.7, shall meet the dimension and shape requirements of Annex 5.
requirements.test_case: Visually inspect the shape and dimensions of the retro-reflector against Annex 5, paragraph 1.

requirements.text: The Class IA or IB retro-reflector, when tested according to paragraph 5.1.7, shall meet the photometric and colorimetric requirements of paragraphs 5.1.4 to 5.1.5.
requirements.test_case: Perform goniophotometric RI and night-time colour measurements per Annex 4 Part 1 and paragraph 4.2.1.

requirements.text: The Class IA or IB retro-reflector, when tested according to paragraph 5.1.7, shall meet the physical and mechanical requirements that apply to the nature of its materials and construction.
requirements.test_case: Run the heat, water, fuel/oil, corrosion, rear-face, stability and weathering tests applicable to the construction.

requirements.text: The retro-reflector shall be subjected to the heat resistance test of Part 1 of Annex 6 (48 consecutive hours in a dry atmosphere at 65 °C ± 2 °C, then 1 h cooling at 23 °C ± 2 °C). At least one hour after this test it shall meet the colour requirements of paragraph 5.1.5 and the RI requirements of paragraph 5.1.4 at an angle of divergence of 20' and an illumination angle β1 = β2 = 0° (or the position defined in Annex 4 Part 1, paragraphs 1.1 and 1.2).
requirements.test_case: Condition the samples for 48 h at 65 °C, cool for 1 h, then measure colour and RI at 20' and 0°/0°.

requirements.text: After the heat resistance test, no cracking or appreciable distortion of the retro-reflector, and in particular of its optical component, shall be visible.
requirements.test_case: Visually inspect the samples for cracks and distortion after the 48 h / 65 °C exposure.

requirements.text: After a satisfactory water penetration test, the retro-reflector shall be subjected to the tests for resistance to motor fuels and lubricating oils (Parts 1 and 2 of Annex 7; 5 min exposure each).
requirements.test_case: Expose the outer surface to the n-heptane/toluol mixture and then to detergent lubricating oil for 5 min each, then inspect and measure colour and RI.

requirements.text: In case the retro-reflector has essential metal components susceptible to corrosion, it shall be subjected to the corrosion test of Part 4 of Annex 6 (24 h exposure, 2 h interval, 24 h exposure).
requirements.test_case: Perform the salt-spray corrosion test per Annex 6 Part 4, then inspect and measure colour and RI.

requirements.text: In case the retro-reflector is mirror-backed with an accessible rear face, it shall be subjected to the abrasive-strength test of the rear face in Part 5 of Annex 6.
requirements.test_case: Brush the rear face and apply the fuel mixture per Annex 6 Part 5, then measure RI.

requirements.text: The retro-reflector shall be subjected to the test for stability in time of its optical properties in Part 3 of Annex 4.
requirements.test_case: Check colour and RI of samples after the stability-in-time assessment per Annex 4 Part 3.

requirements.text: The retro-reflector shall be subjected to the resistance to weathering test of Part 6 of Annex 6 (accelerated artificial weathering per EN ISO 4892-2:2013).
requirements.test_case: Expose the samples in a xenon-arc weathering chamber per EN ISO 4892-2:2013, then measure colour and RI.

requirements.text: After undergoing the tests of paragraph 5.1.3.1, the retro-reflectors in each test group shall have a colour that satisfies paragraph 5.1.5 (red night-time colour per UN R48).
requirements.test_case: Check colour visually after each test group and measure trichromatic coordinates in case of doubt.

requirements.text: After undergoing the tests of paragraph 5.1.3.1, the retro-reflectors in each test group shall have an RI satisfying paragraph 5.1.4. Verification is at an angle of divergence of 20' and an illumination angle β1 = β2 = 0° only, or if necessary in all positions of Annex 4 Part 1, paragraphs 1.1 and 1.2.
requirements.test_case: Measure RI at 20' and 0°/0° after each test group and compare with Table 3 (red: ≥ 300 mcd/lx).

requirements.text: For photometric measurements, only the illuminating surface defined by the planes contiguous to the outermost parts of the retro-reflector's optical system, as indicated by the manufacturer, shall be considered. This surface shall lie within a circle of 200 mm diameter and be limited to 100 cm², although the retro-reflecting optical units need not attain this area.
requirements.test_case: Check on the drawing and sample that the declared illuminating surface lies within a 200 mm circle and is ≤ 100 cm².

requirements.text: When measured as described in paragraph 3 of Part 1 of Annex 4, the RI values of the red Class IA/IB retro-reflector shall be equal to or greater than those of Table 3 (mcd/lx). At divergence 20': 300 at β1=0°/β2=0°, 200 at β1=±10°/β2=0°, 100 at β1=±5°/β2=±20°. At divergence 1°30': 5 at 0°/0°, 2.8 at ±10°/0°, 2.5 at ±5°/±20°.
